blocks.text: 1. Hallucination Detection
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864304-723844452.png

Context Recall closed by weighing when its ground truth comparison is worth measuring directly. Hallucination Detection, catching claims a generated answer invented outright, names and targets the most severe form of the unfaithfulness this module has been building toward.
It flags any claim that has no support anywhere in the retrieved context or the ground truth.
2. Hallucination Is Unfaithfulness At Its Worst

blocks.alt: Hallucination Is Unfaithfulness At Its Worst
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864305-225401100.png
Unfaithful covers any unsupported claim, mild or severe.
Hallucination specifically names the case where the model invented a specific, confident, false-sounding detail.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Term","Scope"],"rows":[["Unfaithful","Any claim not supported by the retrieved context"],["Hallucination","A specific, confidently invented false-sounding detail"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Hallucination Sounds Confident On Purpose
A hallucinated claim is written in the same confident tone as a well grounded one.
Nothing about the surface phrasing distinguishes a hallucination from a supported fact.
4. Detecting Hallucinations Reuses Faithfulness Checking
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864305-108781291.png
The same claim by claim verification is the primary detection technique here.
An unsupported claim identified this way is exactly what gets flagged as a hallucination.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: The same claim decomposition and verification process from Faithfulness is the mechanism hallucination detection uses, just with a stricter label applied to the worst unsupported claims.

blocks.text: 5. Cross Checking Across Multiple Generations
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864305-796263208.png
Generating the same answer several times and comparing them reveals claims that appear inconsistently.
A detail that changes between runs is a strong signal it was invented rather than retrieved.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Detection technique","What it looks for"],"rows":[["Claim by claim verification","Claims with no support in the retrieved context"],["Cross checking generations","Details that change between repeated runs"]]}

blocks.text: 6. A Separate Hallucination Judge Model
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864305-750770100.png
As with reflection requiring a critic, not just execution, in Reflection, a dedicated judge model can be prompted specifically to spot invented details.
A separate evaluative pass distinct from the model that generated the answer being checked.
7. False Positives In Hallucination Detection
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864305-300895366.png
A detection model can itself misjudge a supported claim as unsupported.
Hallucination detection is its own imperfect check, not a guaranteed ground truth.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A judge model incorrectly flagging a well supported claim as invented is a real risk since the detection process itself is another model making a judgment call, not an infallible oracle.

blocks.text: 8. Hallucination Rate Complements Faithfulness
A hallucination rate counts specifically invented claims, a stricter subset of what faithfulness already flags as unsupported.
The two metrics track the same underlying failure at different levels of severity.
9. Recognizing When Dedicated Hallucination Detection Is Worth The Added Cost

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Dedicated Hallucination Detection Is Worth The Added Cost
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447864306-602644097.png
High stakes domains where an invented detail is costly justify dedicated detection.
A low stakes system already tracking faithfulness may not need a separate detection pass.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates flagging an unsupported claim as a hallucination and cross checking it across repeated generations.

code.content:
context = "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month and includes ten projects."

def is_supported(claim, context):
    key_terms = [term for term in claim.lower().split() if len(term) > 4]
    matches = sum(1 for term in key_terms if term in context.lower())
    return matches >= 2

def detect_hallucinations(claims, context):
    # detecting hallucinations reuses faithfulness checking
    return [claim for claim in claims if not is_supported(claim, context)]

def cross_check_generations(generations):
    # cross checking across multiple generations
    all_claims = [set(gen) for gen in generations]
    consistent_claims = set.intersection(*all_claims) if all_claims else set()
    inconsistent_claims = set.union(*all_claims) - consistent_claims
    return consistent_claims, inconsistent_claims

answer_claims = [
    "The Falcon plan costs twenty dollars per month.",
    "The Falcon plan includes ten projects.",
    "The Falcon plan was launched five years ago.",
]

hallucinations = detect_hallucinations(answer_claims, context)
print("Flagged hallucinations:")
for h in hallucinations:
    print(f" {h}")

generation_a = ["Falcon plan costs twenty dollars", "Includes ten projects", "Launched five years ago"]
generation_b = ["Falcon plan costs twenty dollars", "Includes ten projects", "Launched three years ago"]
consistent, inconsistent = cross_check_generations([generation_a, generation_b])
print(f"\nInconsistent across generations: {inconsistent}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the launch date claim both flagged as unsupported by context and inconsistent across repeated generations, exactly the two complementary detection signals.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Treating every unfaithful claim as a hallucination without distinguishing severity.
Trusting a hallucination judge model's output as ground truth without accounting for its own error rate.
Skipping cross-generation checks that could catch inconsistent, likely invented details.
Building dedicated hallucination detection for a low stakes system already served fine by faithfulness alone.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Hallucination detection catches claims a generated answer invented outright.
Hallucination names the severe case of unfaithfulness: a specific, confidently invented false detail.
A hallucinated claim reads with the same confident tone as a supported one.
Claim by claim verification, the same technique behind faithfulness is the primary detection method.
Comparing repeated generations of the same answer reveals claims that appear inconsistently.
A dedicated judge model can be prompted specifically to spot invented details.
Hallucination detection is itself an imperfect check, capable of its own false positives.
Hallucination rate is a stricter subset of what faithfulness already flags as unsupported.
